h1: Maneenaksen Resort Pa Sang, Lamphun — a quiet, budget garden resort among rice paddies and flowers
intro: If you want to escape the bustle for a genuinely quiet corner of rural Lamphun on a tight budget, Maneenaksen Resort in Pa Sang is a good fit · It's a Lanna-style garden resort of about 19 rooms, with wooden houses and concrete bungalows scattered among flower gardens, vegetable plots and jasmine-rice paddies · Rooms have air-conditioning, a fridge, hot water, free Wi-Fi and parking, and there's even a herbal sauna to unwind in · From approx ฿500/night — ideal for self-drivers after a peaceful, low-cost stay near Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha

body.html: Maneenaksen Resort sits at around 720 Moo 1 in Pa Sang District, Lamphun Province · Pa Sang is a small district south of Lamphun town, with a shaded, rural feel of rice paddies and fruit orchards · The resort is about 15–20 minutes' drive from Lamphun's old town and close to Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha, an important hillside temple of Pa Sang · It suits self-drivers best, as public transport here is limited.

The appeal here is that it's a Lanna-style garden resort · About 19 wooden Thai houses and concrete bungalows are spread across a green plot, surrounded by rose gardens, assorted trees, vegetable plots, jasmine-rice paddies and a fruit orchard · Anyone who likes to wake early, stroll the garden, listen to birdsong and photograph rural scenery will enjoy it · This is a place that sells peace and greenery rather than luxury.
"A fairly quiet place, good for anyone who wants calm. Shaded, with gardens all around, inexpensive, and the room was reasonably clean."

Rooms are simple but cover the essentials · There's air-conditioning, a TV, fridge, hot water, a mini-bar, cable and free Wi-Fi · On top of that there are extras you rarely get at this price, such as a herbal sauna, a seminar room and an airport shuttle service · Parking is on site · At rates starting around ฿500/night, that's more than you'd expect from a small rural resort.

To be straight about it, this is an older, simple property · Real guest reviews say the rooms are reasonably clean and the atmosphere is pleasantly quiet, but the buildings and decor show their age — it's not a sleek new resort · Anyone expecting modern boutique rooms, hotel-soft beds or a swimming pool may feel it falls short · But viewed as a garden retreat for a quiet night's rest along the way, it does its job well for the price.

On location, Pa Sang is a fair way from the main sights · From Maneenaksen Resort it's about 15–20 minutes to Wat Phra That Hariphunchai in central Lamphun and roughly 50 minutes to an hour into Chiang Mai city · Pa Sang is known for hand-woven cotton and longan, and during longan season (around July–August) the roadsides fill with orchards · It works best as a quiet base to sleep, then drive out to temples and markets during the day.

On scores and reviews, Maneenaksen Resort still has only a handful of online reviews, as it's a local stay that isn't listed on every major booking platform · From what's there, the main praise is for the quiet, the greenery and the very low price, while the notes are the age of the rooms and a location that needs a car · It's a value pick for the rural-minded, not a place to show off.

In short, Maneenaksen Resort suits self-drivers after a quiet garden stay at a few-hundred-baht rate, in the rural setting of Pa Sang · It's good for couples escaping the city, travellers breaking a Lamphun–Li–Chiang Mai journey, or those visiting Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha · But if you want to stay within the old town and walk to the sights, want a modern room, or want a pool, it's worth comparing options in Lamphun town too.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Maneenaksen Resort Pa Sang, Lamphun

faq.q: Where is Maneenaksen Resort and what's nearby?
faq.a: Maneenaksen Resort is at around 720 Moo 1 in Pa Sang District, Lamphun Province · It's about 10 minutes' drive from Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha and Pa Sang market · Around 15–20 minutes from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and Lamphun old town · And roughly 50–60 minutes into Chiang Mai city.

faq.q: How much does Maneenaksen Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx ฿500/night for a standard air-conditioned room · There are concrete rooms and wooden garden houses, plus family and group rooms, roughly ฿500–1,200 · All rooms have A/C, hot water and free Wi-Fi · As a local stay, it's best to contact them directly for the latest rates.

faq.q: Does it have a swimming pool, and what facilities are there?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool · But rooms have A/C, a TV, fridge, hot water, mini-bar, cable and free Wi-Fi · There's also parking, a herbal sauna, a seminar room and an airport shuttle service — uncommon at this price point.

faq.q: Who is Maneenaksen Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a strong pick for self-drivers who want a quiet garden stay at a budget rate · Good for couples escaping the city, travellers breaking a Lamphun–Li–Chiang Mai journey, or those visiting Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha · It's less ideal for those who want to stay within the old town and walk to the sights, or want a modern room.

faq.q: Is the property dated, and are the rooms clean?
faq.a: Real guest reviews say the buildings and decor show their age, but rooms are reasonably clean and the atmosphere is pleasantly quiet · It's a simple garden resort focused on calm and price, not a sleek new stay — set expectations for a few-hundred-baht budget.

faq.q: Do I need my own car, and how do I book?
faq.a: You'll want your own car, as Pa Sang has limited public transport and few restaurants nearby · It isn't listed on every major booking platform, so it's best to call or message the resort's Facebook to check availability and the latest rates before travelling.
